summary: Adversarially review the Korean paper draft: number consistency, overclaim/honesty, venue-quality flow, citation accuracy; return a prioritized edit list

reviews.aspect: Number & statistics consistency + honesty review of docs/novel_research/PAPER_DRAFT_ko.md against the five verified result JSONs
severity_issues: SIGNIFICANCE MISATTRIBUTION IN ABSTRACT (most serious). The abstract says the proposed bank-prior correction is 'high-power statistically significant (p<0.01)'. But the 'proposed' row in Table 1 (bolded, gold 0.760) is the CSLS variant, whose high-power gain over the matched-grid hybrid is only +0.0033 with p=0.6003 (NOT significant; final_suite.json csls +bm25 lora384 synth_vs_lora384_bm25_repro=[0.0033, 0.6003]). The ONLY variant with a significant high-power gain is modality-gap (+0.0057, p=0.0). Observation 3 in the body correctly attributes significance to modality-gap, but the abstract attaches it to 'the proposed correction' generally, implying the headline CSLS method is significant when it is a tie. This reads as claiming a significant win where the data for the headline method shows a wash.

'CONSISTENT POSITIVE' OVERSTATED FOR THE BANK-PRIOR FAMILY. Observation 3 / abstract call the bank-prior gain 'small but consistent (작지만 일관된)'. For the proposed CSLS row this is only technically true (gold +0.039, multi-pos +0.018, high-power +0.003 NON-significant p=0.60). Across the bank-prior family the high-power direction is NOT consistent: qbnorm_mul high-power delta is -0.0001 (p=1.0) and qbnorm_dis is +0.0065 (p=0.09, n.s.). Only modality-gap is reliably positive at high power. Calling the effect 'consistent' while the headline method's high-power gain is an insignificant +0.003 overstates robustness.

TABLE 3 GME+BM25 P-VALUE MISLABEL/OVERCLAIM. Table 3 reports GME+BM25 gold loss as 'sign p<0.001'. The actual SIGN-test p in gme_baseline.json (human30_gme_bm25_vs_lora_bm25_pub[MRR]) is sign_test_p=0.0044, i.e. p<0.01, NOT p<0.001. The p<0.001 value is the one-sided bootstrap p (p_delta_gt0=0.0), a different test than the 'sign' label used for the GME-dense row (sign p=0.007, which does match its sign test). Either relabel as bootstrap or correct to p<0.01. The GME-dense entry 'sign p=0.007' is correct.

SECTION 6.1 FAILURE ANALYSIS IS APPLIED TO A DIFFERENT PIPELINE THAN THE HEADLINE PROPOSED METHOD, with ambiguous wording. 6.1 says 'the current best pipeline (현 최강 파이프라인) misses exactly 3 (answer ranks 191, 378, 483)'. Those three catastrophic ranks belong to lora384_bm25_pub (the best-tuned 0.756 pipeline; refs.json/llm_reranker.json), NOT the proposed CSLS pipeline whose gold ranks max out at 39 (no rank >=100; final_suite csls +bm25 lora384 eval_ranks). Since Table 1's bolded best is the 0.760 CSLS proposed method, '현 최강 파이프라인' here silently switches referent. As written it could imply the proposed method also catastrophically fails on those 3 queries, which is false.
concrete_edits: Abstract, the clause '고검정력 합성 평가 +0.003–0.006), 고검정력 평가에서 통계적으로 유의하다(p<0.01)': split the attribution. Replace with something like '고검정력 합성 평가에서 modality-gap 변형은 +0.0057로 통계적으로 유의(p<0.01)하나, 표 1의 헤드라인 변형(CSLS)의 고검정력 이득(+0.003)은 유의하지 않다.' Do not let 'the proposed correction ... is significant at high power' stand unqualified.

Abstract, '작지만 일관된 개선을 주며': qualify to 'modality-gap 변형에서 작지만 고검정력에서 유의한 개선', and note that the CSLS headline variant's high-power gain is a non-significant +0.003 / the gold +0.039 gain is not significant (p=0.11).

Abstract, 'matched-grid 하이브리드 대비 gold MRR +0.039': add a one-line caveat that a separately best-tuned hybrid reaches gold 0.756 and the proposed (0.760) is a statistical tie with it (this caveat currently exists only in Observation 3, not the abstract).
Table 3, GME-Qwen2VL-2B + BM25 row, '패배 (sign p<0.001)': change to 'sign p=0.004' (or relabel the column to 'bootstrap p' if you intend p_delta_gt0=0.0). The verified sign-test p is 0.0044.

Section 6.1, '현 최강 파이프라인은 30개 중 정확히 3개를 심하게 놓친다(정답 rank 191·378·483)': specify the pipeline explicitly, e.g. 'best-tuned 하이브리드(0.756, LoRA+BM25)는 ...' and add a sentence that the proposed CSLS 파이프라인(0.760)은 동일 쿼리에서 최악 rank가 39로 이 셋을 심하게 놓치지 않는다 — to avoid implying the headline method fails. Reconcile the 'current best' terminology between Table 1 (0.760 proposed) and 6.1 (0.756 best-tuned).

Section 6.4, '(0.856→0.911)': this mixes the BASE no-rerank multipos (0.856) with the PURE/aggressive reranker multipos (0.9111), while the surrounding sentence discusses the TUNED reranker (whose multipos is 0.909). Either state '0.856→0.909 (tuned)' to match the sentence, or explicitly say the figure is for the aggressive 'pure' variant. As written it stitches two different variants' numbers.
minor_issues: Verified consistent (no change needed): Table 1 all four MRR rows match the JSONs after rounding — zero-shot 0.571/0.655/0.431, LoRA 0.684/0.794/0.568, matched-grid hybrid 0.721/0.858/0.903, proposed CSLS 0.760/0.876/0.906; gold CIs match; mgap multi-pos 0.878 / high-power 0.908; mgap synth gain +0.0057 p<0.01. Observation 1 (LoRA vs zero-shot high-power 0.568 vs 0.431, 905 wins/257 losses, p~0) and Observation 2 (+BM25 0.568->0.903, +0.334, p~0) both match. GME gold 0.467/0.452, high-power 0.430/0.780 all match. Split-overlap 6/1706=0.35% arithmetic correct.

Q4 (leakage) — clean. Sections 3.3/3.4 explicitly select all hyperparameters (lambda, k, beta, w, n) on train-split synthetic validation only and estimate distribution stats from bank/gallery, not eval queries; the 2-product split-overlap is footnoted with equal exposure across methods. No leakage-implying claim found.

Q1 (matched-grid vs best-tuned framing) — broadly honest. The matched-grid 0.721 is the genuine apples-to-apples baseline (same BM25 grid as every +BM25 row), and the stronger 0.756 best-tuned hybrid is disclosed in Observation 3 with an explicit 'statistical tie, no superiority claimed'. The baseline is not weakened to inflate the gain. Only residual gap is that the abstract omits the 0.756 caveat (see concrete edits).

Observation 3 gold stats for CSLS proposed: '+0.039 (8승/2패, p=0.11)' matches final_suite eval_vs_lora384_bm25_repro=[0.0391, 0.109, 8, 2] (0.109 rounds to 0.11). The 'statistical tie with 0.756' claim matches eval_vs_lora384_bm25_pub=[0.0042, 0.727].
The learned-reranker numbers in 6.2 (val 0.88+, gold 0.504) are not present in the five verified JSONs and could not be cross-checked; they are not contradicted by available data but are unverified.
reviews.overall: All headline Table 1 / Table 3 numbers and the main observation deltas are numerically accurate against the on-disk JSONs (after rounding). The honesty concerns are not about wrong numbers but about how significance is attributed. The single must-fix issue is the abstract's claim that the proposed bank-prior correction is high-power significant at p<0.01: the bolded 'proposed' method in Table 1 is the CSLS variant, whose high-power gain over the matched-grid hybrid is a non-significant +0.0033 (p=0.60); only the modality-gap variant is significant (+0.0057, p<0.01). Observation 3 in the body states this correctly, but the abstract conflates the two and over-attributes significance to the headline method. Relatedly, the 'small but consistent' framing overstates robustness given the bank-prior family is not consistently positive at high power (qbnorm_mul -0.0001, qbnorm_dis n.s.). Two secondary fixes: Table 3 mislabels GME+BM25's loss as 'sign p<0.001' (actual sign-test p=0.0044, i.e. <0.01), and Section 6.1's failure analysis ('ranks 191/378/483') is silently applied to the 0.756 best-tuned pipeline rather than the 0.760 proposed pipeline (which has no rank worse than 39), with ambiguous '현 최강 파이프라인' wording. The matched-grid-vs-best-tuned baseline framing is otherwise honest (the strong 0.756 baseline is disclosed and the proposed method is explicitly called a tie with it), and there are no leakage-implying claims.

reviews.aspect: Structure, flow, and contribution framing (NeurIPS/ICLR adversarial reviewer persona)
severity_issues: BAIT-AND-SWITCH ON THE HEADLINE METHOD (most damaging to accept-ability). Table 1's 'proposed (C2)' row is the CSLS-selected correction (Gold 0.760). But CSLS's gain over the matched-grid hybrid is NOT significant on the only powered eval: synth sign test 69 wins / 62 losses, p=0.60 (verified from final_suite.json synth_vs_lora384_bm25_repro=[0.0033,...,69,62]). The ONLY statistically significant correction gain (+0.0057, sign p<1e-5) belongs to modality_gap (86/37), a DIFFERENT operator demoted to a parenthetical. A reviewer reading Abstract+Table 1 will believe 'the proposed bank-prior method gives a significant high-power gain'; that is true only if 'the method' = modality-gap, but the headline number (0.760) = CSLS, whose high-power gain is null. This conflation reads as cherry-picking the highest gold number (CSLS, p=0.11 vs hybrid) while borrowing significance from a different operator. This is the single biggest reject risk for overclaiming.

ABSTRACT OVERSTATES C2 AS A UNIFORM WIN. Abstract: 'matched-grid 하이브리드 대비 gold MRR +0.039, multi-positive +0.018, 고검정력 +0.003–006... 고검정력 평가에서 통계적으로 유의.' None of gold (+0.039, p=0.11) or multi-pos (+0.018, sign p=0.69, verified multipos.json csls_bm25_vs_dense_bm25 sign_test_p=0.6875) is significant; only ONE operator's high-power delta is. The abstract presents three positive deltas as if they are the contribution's evidence, when two of three are non-significant and the significant one is from a different operator than the 0.039/0.018 ones. A careful reviewer will read this as the classic 'consistent positive deltas' overclaim over an underpowered eval.

C2 NOVELTY IS THINLY DIFFERENTIATED FROM QB-Norm/CSLS — 'what EXACTLY is new' is never pinned down. The method (§3.3) literally applies CSLS (Conneau 2018) and QB-Norm/Dynamic Inverted Softmax (Bogolin 2022) verbatim; the only delta vs prior work is the SOURCE of the query bank (reused training synth queries instead of a held-out/real query bank). QB-Norm already uses a query bank to estimate gallery hubness — so 'apply hubness norm with a query bank' is exactly prior art. The genuinely new claim ('the bank can be the SAME synthetic queries used for LoRA training, at zero extra cost') is real but small, and is currently buried. As written, a reviewer can say 'C2 = QB-Norm with a different bank source, +0.003 non-significant for the headlined variant' and reject for thinness. The contribution must be reframed as a narrow, honest observation, not a methodological novelty.

C1/C2/C3 OVERLAP AND C3 SWALLOWS THE PAPER. C3 (evaluation methodology + ceiling diagnosis + GME negative) is doing more work than C1/C2 combined and is where all the significant/interesting results live (LoRA p~0; ceiling=labeling artifact; GME loses). Meanwhile C2 (the claimed 'novelty') is the weakest, non-significant-for-the-headline contribution. The framing inverts the actual strength: the paper sells 'bank-as-prior novelty' but its real, defensible contributions are (a) the distribution-gap recipe works hard (C1) and (b) the multi-protocol eval shows the gold ceiling is a labeling artifact (C3). A reviewer will feel the abstract's emphasis is misallocated.
concrete_edits: DEMOTE C2 FROM 'novelty' TO 'a free, consistent-but-mostly-non-significant add-on,' and STOP headlining CSLS. In Abstract replace '제안하는 뤄크-prior 보정은 ... 고검정력 평가에서 통계적으로 유의하다(p<0.01)' with something like: '하나의 보정 변형(modality-gap)은 고검정력 평가에서 작지만 유의한 +0.0057(sign p<0.01) 이득을 주며, 나머지 변형과 gold/multi-pos 델타는 양의 방향이나 유의하지 않다.' Be explicit that the headline-gold variant (CSLS) is NOT significant on the powered eval.

MAKE TABLE 1's PROPOSED ROW INTERNALLY HONEST. Either (a) report modality-gap as the proposed correction everywhere (Gold 0.734, synth 0.908, the significant one) instead of CSLS (Gold 0.760, synth 0.906, non-significant), so the headline number and the significance come from the SAME operator; or (b) keep both but add a column 'high-power sign-test p vs matched-grid hybrid' showing CSLS p=0.60, mgap p<0.001 — so the reader cannot conflate them. Option (a) is cleaner and removes the bait-and-switch. The current footnote '(modality-gap 변형은 ... 더 높음)' is not enough.

REWRITE THE C2 NOVELTY SENTENCE TO STATE EXACTLY WHAT IS NEW. Replace §1 (C2) and §3.3's framing with one crisp differentiation: 'Unlike QB-Norm (Bogolin 2022), which assumes access to a representative query bank, we observe that the synthetic queries already generated for LoRA training serve as such a bank for free — no held-out queries, no extra generation, no extra labels. Our contribution is this reuse + the empirical finding of its (limited) effect size, NOT the normalization operator itself.' Explicitly disclaim operator novelty in Related Work §2 so reviewers can't accuse you of hiding it.

RE-BALANCE THE CONTRIBUTION LIST so the abstract leads with what is actually strong and significant. Lead C1 (LoRA dominance, p~0, two evals) and the C3 ceiling-diagnosis (mean 5.07 positives → gold ceiling is a labeling artifact) as the primary results; present bank-prior reuse as a secondary 'free add-on' finding, not as 'novelty.' This single re-emphasis is the change most likely to flip a borderline reviewer, because the paper's honest core (recipe works + eval methodology) is genuinely solid and currently undersold.

ADD THE MISSING PROBLEM FIGURE the reader expects. There is no figure at all. Add Figure 1: a side-by-side of (a) a ~500-char formal GPT-4o caption vs (b) a ~50-char user query for the SAME product, plus a t-SNE/PCA of caption embeddings vs user-query embeddings vs image embeddings showing the modality/distribution gap. This directly motivates both C1 and C2 and is the single most expected visual for a 'distribution gap is the dominant weakness' paper.

ADD THE MAIN COMPARISON FIGURE/PANEL a reviewer expects: a forest plot of the four ladder steps with bootstrap 95% CIs on all three protocols (gold/multi-pos/high-power). The CIs are already computed (final_suite.json eval_MRR_ci, synth_MRR_ci). This makes the 'gold is underpowered, high-power is decisive' argument visual and pre-empts the 'you are reading noise' critique.

FIX THE STAT-LABEL PRECISION in Observation 1 & 3. Obs 1 says 'paired sign test p~0 (905승/257패)' — verify wording: 905/257 is the synth win/loss count and the reported value is p_delta_gt0 (bootstrap), not a sign test; either relabel as 'bootstrap p~0' or report the actual sign-test p. Same issue in Obs 3: the '+0.0057, p<0.01' is correct as a SIGN test (I verified 86/37 → p=1.2e-5) but the JSON's 0.0 next to it is p_delta_gt0; make sure the paper consistently names which test produced which p so a stats-literate reviewer doesn't catch a mislabel.

STATE THE HIGH-POWER EVAL's CIRCULARITY MORE PROMINENTLY, not just in §7. The 1,706 synth queries are generated by the same family of local LLM prompts used to build the training bank; +BM25 wins partly because synth queries share lexical surface with metadata (you already note 0.90+ inflation). Since C1's headline significance (p~0) and the +BM25 'single strongest lever' claim both rest on this eval, a reviewer will worry the high-power eval flatters exactly the components you advocate. Add one sentence in §5 (not buried in §7) acknowledging that high-power significance for lexical/synthetic-aligned methods should be read as a lower-bound-of-doubt, and that the human-30 multi-pos eval is the bias check.
minor_issues: GME 'citation 140' (§6.3) — wf5_lit_2025_2026.json says '140회' for GME but elsewhere lists a 'citation_count_verified: 176' figure; pin the source/date for the 140 so a reviewer can't flag a stale number. Citation counts also date a paper badly; consider dropping the raw count and saying 'a widely-cited 2024/2025 VLM embedder.'
Title is overlong and front-loads the weakest contribution ('학습용 합성 쿼리 뤄크의 추론 시점 재활용'). Consider leading with the distribution-alignment story, which is the strong result.

§3.3 CSLS formula: r_T(q) and r_G(g) defined as top-k means; standard CSLS uses mean of k nearest neighbors — fine, but state k is the SAME val-selected k for both terms or two separate ks, and note the bank (not eval queries) is used for r_G to make the no-leakage claim airtight.

§6.4 lists '950개 파이프라인' combo search but combos.json only exposes a topk list; ensure the appendix actually documents the 950-config grid or soften the count. Multiple-comparisons over 950 pipelines selected on val then reported on a 30-query gold is itself a defensibility risk a reviewer may raise — pre-empt with 'all selection on val, gold reported once.'

'split overlap 2 products (6/1706=0.35%)' is footnoted as harmless; a strict reviewer may still want the high-power numbers recomputed with those 6 queries removed to fully close the leakage door — cheap to do and removes an attack surface.

Multi-positive labels are LLM-judged (blind) — §7 admits noise but the ceiling-diagnosis (C3(b)) leans heavily on 'mean 5.07 positives.' Add an inter-rater or human-spot-check on a subset (even n=5 queries) to keep a reviewer from dismissing the central diagnosis as LLM-label circularity.
reviews.overall: All numbers in the draft verify exactly against the ground-truth JSONs (Table 1: CSLS+BM25 lora384 gold 0.7602/multipos 0.8761/synth 0.9059; gold delta +0.0391 sign p=0.109 8w/2l; mgap synth +0.0057 sign p=1.2e-5; GME losses all framings) — there is no fabrication and no leakage-implying claim, which is a real strength. The problem is FRAMING, not data. As a top-venue reviewer I would currently lean reject for overclaiming + thinness of the headlined contribution, but it is a fixable borderline. The fatal framing flaw is a bait-and-switch: the abstract and Table 1 headline the bank-prior correction via the CSLS variant (best gold = 0.760) while the only statistically significant high-power gain belongs to a DIFFERENT operator (modality-gap, +0.0057); the headlined CSLS variant's high-power gain is null (sign p=0.60). This lets the abstract imply a significant, consistent 'novel' win that the headlined method does not actually deliver, and the 'bank-as-prior' novelty is thinly differentiated from QB-Norm/CSLS (same operators; only the bank source is new). SINGLE CHANGE THAT MOST IMPROVES ACCEPT-ABILITY: stop selling C2 as 'novelty,' demote it to a small honest 'free, mostly-non-significant add-on,' make the headlined operator and the significant operator the SAME (use modality-gap throughout), and re-lead the abstract with the genuinely strong, defensible results — C1 (LoRA dominance, p~0 on two evals) and C3's ceiling-is-a-labeling-artifact diagnosis (mean 5.07 valid positives). Also essential and currently missing: a Figure 1 problem illustration (formal caption vs short user query + embedding-gap plot) and a forest-plot main comparison with the already-computed bootstrap CIs across all three protocols. Files: draft /root/code/jolnon/docs/novel_research/PAPER_DRAFT_ko.md; ground truth /root/code/jolnon/output/novel/{final_suite,multipos,combos,gme_baseline,llm_reranker}.json.

severity_issues: TITLE ERROR (Liang et al., References line 165): the draft writes 'Mind the Gap: Understanding the Modality Gap in Contrastive Representation Learning.' The correct title is 'Mind the Gap: Understanding the Modality Gap in MULTI-MODAL Contrastive Representation Learning.' The word 'Multi-modal' is dropped. Verified against NeurIPS 2022 / arXiv:2203.02053 (authors Liang, Zhang, Kwon, Yeung, Zou). Venue (NeurIPS 2022) is correct; only the title string is wrong. This is the single hard citation-string error in the bibliography.

MISSING KEY RELATED WORK for the C2 framing (query-bank-as-distribution-prior). The draft's headline novelty is 'reusing the synthetic-query bank as a test-time hubness/gap prior,' yet it cites only QB-Norm and CSLS for hubness. Liang et al. is cited for the modality gap PHENOMENON, but no citation grounds the modality-gap MEAN-SUBTRACTION correction the draft actually applies in 3.3 / Table-1 ('modality-gap+BM25'). wf1 (shortlist rank 4) explicitly attributes this operator to the same Liang et al. NeurIPS 2022 'Mind the Gap' work (mean-shift along the gap vector). As written, the modality-gap correction operator (a Table-1 row and a claimed-significant +0.0057 result) has no method citation. Add the Liang et al. cite at the point in 3.3 where the gap-centering operator is introduced, not only in the phenomenon sentence in 2.
concrete_edits: References line 165 (Liang et al.): change 'Mind the Gap: Understanding the Modality Gap in Contrastive Representation Learning. NeurIPS 2022.' to 'Mind the Gap: Understanding the Modality Gap in Multi-modal Contrastive Representation Learning. NeurIPS 2022. arXiv:2203.02053.'

Section 3.3 (modality-gap centering bullet, line 55) and Table-1 footnote (line 96): add an explicit citation '(Liang et al., NeurIPS 2022)' to the modality-gap mean-subtraction operator, since this is the source of the correction the paper reports as statistically significant (+0.0057, p<0.01) but currently cites nowhere as a method.

References consistency: several entries carry arXiv IDs (SigLIP 2, QB-Norm, CSLS, Promptriever, E5-V, GME, VLM2Vec, MM-Embed, ColPali, DSE, ColBERT) but others omit them (Liang et al., LoRA has ID but no year, Doc2Query, InPars, Promptagator, HyDE, BM25). Either add IDs/years uniformly or drop them uniformly. Concretely: 'Hu et al. LoRA. arXiv:2106.09685.' has no year (add 2021/ICLR 2022); Doc2Query 'Nogueira & Lin. 2019.' is fine but the canonical docTTTTTquery tech report is 2019/2020 - keep '2019' (defensible). HyDE 'Gao et al. ACL 2023' verified correct (arXiv:2212.10496); optionally add the ID.

Optional MISSING related work (only if a referee on synthetic-query training is expected): the synthetic-query-generation paragraph (line 31) cites Doc2Query/InPars/Promptagator/Promptriever but omits SWIM-IR (multilingual LLM-synthetic-query pipeline) and mmE5 (multilingual MLLM synthetic-data embeddings). wf5 flags mmE5 (ACL 2025 Findings, 41 cites) as the single MOST thematically aligned paper to this exact 'train on LLM-generated multilingual user-style queries' recipe. It is below the project's 50-cite bar but is the strongest multilingual precedent; consider a one-line cite to pre-empt 'why no multilingual synthetic-query baseline' critique. Not load-bearing.

Optional: the hubness paragraph (line 33) could note that QB-Norm's dynamic gate is the 'Dynamic Inverted Softmax (DIS)' variant the paper actually uses (per wf1 implement-now item), tightening the attribution; current text says 'QB-Norm/Dynamic Inverted Softmax' which is acceptable but the References entry lists only 'QB-Norm' without naming DIS.
minor_issues: Internal source inconsistency (NOT a draft error): wf5_lit_2025_2026.json cites QB-Norm as both 'CVPR 2022' (line 189) and 'CVPR 2021, 126 cites' (line 192). I web-verified the true venue is CVPR 2022 (openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2022, arXiv:2112.12777). The draft and wf1 both say CVPR 2022, which is CORRECT. No draft edit needed; flagging so the 'CVPR 2021' figure in the prior-research prose is not propagated.

All other venue/year/arXiv-ID citations in the draft verified CORRECT against wf5/wf1 and web: SigLIP 2 (Tschannen, arXiv:2502.14786, 2025); CSLS (Conneau, ICLR 2018, arXiv:1710.04087); Promptagator (Dai, ICLR 2023, web-confirmed); Promptriever (Weller, ICLR 2025, arXiv:2409.11136); E5-V (Jiang, arXiv:2407.12580, 2024); GME (Zhang, arXiv:2412.16855, 2024); VLM2Vec (Jiang, ICLR 2025, arXiv:2410.05160); MM-Embed (Lin, ICLR 2025, arXiv:2411.02571); ColPali (Faysse, ICLR 2025, arXiv:2407.01449); DSE (Ma, EMNLP 2024, arXiv:2406.11251); LamRA body-text 'CVPR 2025' (wf5-confirmed); HyDE (Gao, ACL 2023). No mis-attributed venue/year among these.

Idea characterization check: E5-V characterized as 'text-pairs-only training suffices' (line 35) - matches wf5 verified core idea. ColPali 'patch MaxSim late-interaction', DSE 'single-vector screenshot' (line 37) - both match wf5. GME described as '2024/2025 영향력 있는 VLM 임베더, 인용 140' (line 130) - 140 matches wf5-verified S2 count; GME is a Dec-2024 arXiv (not yet a published venue), so 'arXiv 2024' would be marginally more precise than implying a 2025 venue, but the draft only says 'evaluated as a modern baseline' which is fine.

Number spot-check (related-work-adjacent): GME table §6.3 all match JSON - dense Gold 0.467 (0.4666), High-power 0.430 (0.4299), +BM25 Gold 0.452 (0.4517), +BM25 High-power 0.780 (0.7798). 'GME-dense 0.467 < zero-shot SigLIP2 0.571' framing correct. No overclaim in the negative-evidence section.
reviews.overall: Related Work and References are in good shape for a capstone-tier paper: of ~16 references I verified every venue/year/arXiv-ID and found exactly ONE hard error - the Liang et al. 'Mind the Gap' title drops the word 'Multi-modal'. Venues and years are otherwise all correct (QB-Norm CVPR 2022, Promptagator ICLR 2023, Promptriever/VLM2Vec/MM-Embed/ColPali ICLR 2025, DSE EMNLP 2024, HyDE ACL 2023, CSLS ICLR 2018, SigLIP 2 Tschannen 2025 - all confirmed). No method is mischaracterized; the GME citation count (140) and all GME result numbers match the verified JSONs. The one substantive gap is a MISSING METHOD CITATION: the modality-gap mean-subtraction operator the paper actually runs (and reports as significant, +0.0057 p<0.01) is grounded only by a phenomenon-level mention of Liang et al. in Related Work, not at the operator in Section 3.3 - per the prior research (wf1 shortlist), that same Liang et al. NeurIPS 2022 paper IS the source of the mean-shift correction, so the cite should be moved/duplicated to 3.3. Optional: a one-line cite to SWIM-IR or mmE5 would round out the multilingual synthetic-query lineage, and arXiv-ID formatting is inconsistent across the bibliography. must_fix: ABSTRACT — fix the significance misattribution (the single most serious issue, flagged independently by Reviews 1 and 2 and verified in final_suite.json). The abstract currently says the proposed bank-prior correction gives gains '+0.003–0.006' and is 'statistically significant (p<0.01)' at high power. But the bolded 'proposed' row in Table 1 is the CSLS variant, whose high-power gain over the matched-grid hybrid is +0.0033 with p=0.6003 (NOT significant; synth_vs_lora384_bm25_repro=[0.0033, 0.6003, 69, 62]). The ONLY variant with a significant high-power gain is modality-gap (+0.0057, sign p≈1e-5; synth_vs_lora384_bm25_repro=[0.0057, 0.0, 86, 37]). Rewrite to split the attribution explicitly, e.g.: 'modality-gap 변형은 고검정력 평가에서 +0.0057로 통계적으로 유의(sign p<0.01)하나, 표 1의 헤드라인 변형(CSLS)의 고검정력 이득(+0.003)은 유의하지 않다(p=0.60).' Do NOT let 'the proposed correction ... is significant at high power' stand unqualified.

ABSTRACT — qualify '작지만 일관된(small but consistent)'. The bank-prior family is NOT consistently positive at high power: qbnorm_mul high-power delta is -0.0001 (p=1.0) and qbnorm_dis is +0.0065 (p=0.09, n.s.); only modality-gap is reliably positive and significant. Restrict the 'consistent/significant' claim to the modality-gap variant, and state that the CSLS headline variant's gold +0.039 gain is not significant (p=0.11) and its high-power +0.003 gain is not significant (p=0.60).

The abstract reports 'matched-grid 하이브리드 대비 gold MRR +0.039' but omits that a separately best-tuned hybrid reaches gold 0.756 and the proposed 0.760 is a statistical tie with it (eval_vs_lora384_bm25_pub=[0.0042, 0.727]). The three catastrophic ranks (191, 378, 483) belong to the lora384_bm25_pub 0.756 best-tuned pipeline as reranked (verified in llm_reranker.json pure/tuned ranks), NOT the proposed CSLS 0.760 pipeline, whose gold eval_ranks max out at 39 (no rank ≥100; verified in final_suite.json). The word 'Multi-modal' is dropped (verified against NeurIPS 2022 / arXiv:2203.02053). This is the one hard citation-string error.

final.verdict: After must-fixes the draft is honest and defensible for its stated capstone bar ('beat the chosen baseline on the chosen eval'), and I verified every headline number against the five JSONs — Table 1 (zero-shot 0.571/0.655/0.431, LoRA 0.684/0.794/0.568, matched-grid hybrid 0.721/0.858/0.903, proposed CSLS 0.760/0.876/0.906), Table 3 (GME numbers), Observations 1–2, mean 5.07 positives, and the 0.35% split overlap all check out. There is NO fabrication and NO leakage-implying claim — the problem is framing and attribution, not data. The dominant risk, flagged independently by all three reviewers and confirmed in final_suite.json, is the abstract/Table-1 bait-and-switch: the headlined CSLS variant's high-power gain is a non-significant +0.003 (p=0.60) while significance actually belongs to a different operator (modality-gap, +0.0057, p<0.01), so the abstract over-attributes significance to the headline method and overstates 'consistent.' This plus the three smaller number/citation/referent errors (Table 3 GME+BM25 sign p, §6.1 pipeline ambiguity, Liang title + missing §3.3 method cite, §6.4 spliced 0.856→0.911) are all that make the paper currently wrong-as-written. Fixing the abstract attribution, unifying the headline and significant operator in Table 1, and re-leading with the genuinely strong C1/C3 results clears the defensibility floor and removes the top-venue reviewer's main reject lever; the should-fix items (Figure 1, forest plot, C2 novelty framing, multiple-comparisons pre-emption) raise it from 'defensible' to 'comfortably acceptable.' Remaining residual risk after fixes: the high-power eval's lexical/synthetic circularity, which the paper should acknowledge up front rather than rely on but which is not fatal.
